name: gplcver
why: A 2001-era Verilog simulator is a genuine old-school hardware description environment worth a long afternoon.

brief.what_it_is: GPL Cver is an open-source, interpreted Verilog simulator, listed on SourceForge under Simulation and Electronic Design Automation (EDA). According to the project page, it aims for a feature set and performance similar to Verilog-XL, a commercial simulator. It implements all IEEE 1364-1995 features plus some Verilog-2001 features and has full support for Verilog PLIs. The input is Verilog HDL source. The output is simulation results; the page does not say what form they take. The Homebrew entry names the executable as cver. The SourceForge page lists Linux and Mac as supported operating systems and a console/terminal user interface.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives no explicit motivation beyond providing an open-source alternative to a Verilog-XL-class simulator under the GPL. The Homebrew description calls it a Pragmatic C Software GPL Cver 2001 release, but the homepage text I read does not repeat that attribution or date.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes the simulator as interpreted rather than compiled, and says it supports the Verilog PLI interface. It does not explain the internal mechanism further.
brief.install_notes: No install instructions, build steps, configuration, or first-run guidance appeared in the text I could read. The page is a SourceForge project listing with a Download button and a Files tab, but I did not follow those. Homebrew is the only install path I know of from the brief.
brief.standout: It is a free, GPL-licensed Verilog simulator aimed at Verilog-XL-level feature parity and PLI compatibility, which is unusual for an open-source tool in this niche. Compared with Icarus Verilog, which the same SourceForge page recommends, GPL Cver positions itself on interpreted simulation and PLI support rather than on a compiler architecture.
brief.status: Unverified. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2024-07-17 and Registered 2009-04-24, and it lists 11 downloads this week. I did not check a release history, commit log, or README note, so I cannot tell whether it is maintained or quiet. The page's 2024 update date suggests it is not abandoned.
brief.caveats: I did not reach a README or documentation; the homepage is a SourceForge project page full of site boilerplate, so the install and usage details here are thin. Only Linux and Mac are listed as supported systems. Language support stops at IEEE 1364-1995 plus some Verilog-2001 features, so there is no SystemVerilog. The project has only 2 user reviews, with an average of 5.0 out of 5. The Homebrew description's 2001 date and 'Pragmatic C Software' attribution are not confirmed by the page I read. The scout note about a long afternoon is editorial and not something the source says.
quotes: Open-source interpreted Verilog simulator with a feature set and performance similar to Verilog-XL.
Implements all IEEE 1364-1995 features along with some Verilog-2001 features. Full support for Verilog PLIs.
GPL Cver is a great open-source Verilog simulator.
fetch_log: https://gplcver.sourceforge.net/ : fetched and returned, but the content is a SourceForge project page with heavy boilerplate. The description, license, OS, last-update date, and two user reviews were extractable. No README, docs link, or command examples were found, so I did not follow any further links.
